name: Strix
summary: Autonomous multi-agent AI pentester that runs targets dynamically in a sandbox, validates findings with working proofs-of-concept, and can scan in CI/CD. Open-source core with separate paid cloud and enterprise editions.
notes: Commercial editions exist; the free open-source edition is the Apache-2.0 repo. About 72k stars on 2026-11-07.

name: Shannon
summary: White-box AI pentester for web apps and APIs: reads source code, maps attack paths, then exploits the running app and reports only exploit-confirmed findings (PDF, Markdown, SARIF).
notes: AGPL-3.0 (strong copyleft; network use triggers source-sharing). Keygraph sells Pro/Enterprise editions and offers commercial licensing. Not accepting external code contributions. About 49k stars.

name: PentAGI
summary: Self-hosted fully autonomous multi-agent penetration-testing system (Go backend, web UI) that plans and runs security tools inside Docker.
notes: Repo also ships EULA.md and NOTICE files alongside the MIT LICENSE; read them before commercial reuse. About 32k stars.

name: PentestGPT
summary: Early, widely cited LLM-driven penetration-testing agent framework; accompanied by a USENIX Security 2024 paper.

name: HexStrike AI
summary: MCP server that lets AI clients drive 150+ security tools through a team of specialised agents.

name: CAI (Cybersecurity AI)
summary: Open framework for building cybersecurity agents with hierarchical multi-agent patterns, aimed at bug bounty and autonomous pentesting; basis of several research papers.
notes: Archived status comes from a third-party landscape list; confirm on repo.

name: PentestAgent (GHOSTCREW)
summary: Agent framework for black-box security testing covering bug bounty, red-team and pentest workflows; backed by an AsiaCCS 2025 paper.

name: Pentest-Swarm-AI
summary: Go-based autonomous pentest platform where agents coordinate through a shared blackboard; supports cloud and local models and exposes an MCP server.

name: hackingBuddyGPT
summary: Minimal research framework showing how little code is needed to have an LLM assist with ethical-hacking tasks such as Linux privilege escalation.

name: cochise
summary: Research agent for autonomous assumed-breach penetration testing of Active Directory networks (ACM TOSEM 2025).

name: VulnBot
summary: Multi-agent collaborative pentesting framework built around a penetration task graph; academic project.

name: ctf-agent (Veria Labs)
summary: Autonomous CTF-solving agent that runs several models in parallel; reported first place at the BSidesSF 2026 CTF.

name: Vigil
summary: Open-source agentic SOC with a dozen specialist agents (triage, investigation, hunting, forensics, threat intel, malware and network analysis), Markdown playbooks and MCP-based integrations. Keeps a human approving response actions.
notes: License taken from the project's own wiki; confirm on repo.

name: Agentic SOC Platform
summary: Open-source security-operations platform combining SOAR playbooks with LLM agents for alert-to-case convergence, investigation, enrichment and knowledge capture; integrates Splunk and ELK.

name: Autonomous AI SOC Analyst
summary: Tier-1 SOC agent that ingests Sysmon, CloudTrail and Zeek telemetry, enriches indicators, builds an attack graph and issues a true/false-positive verdict with containment suggestions. Runs with a local LLM via Ollama.

name: AI-Powered SOC Alert Triage Agent
summary: Capstone-style triage agent built on Hermes Agent: selectively enriches IOCs with free threat-intel APIs, maps behaviour to MITRE ATT&CK and outputs a ranked triage report.

name: AI Agent SOC Triage
summary: Python triage agent that classifies alerts against MITRE ATT&CK, scores severity, extracts IOCs and can run response playbooks; works with Splunk, Sentinel and Elastic.

name: AI-SOC (research implementation)
summary: Dockerised reference implementation of an LLM-augmented SOC covering alert triage, RAG-based threat intelligence over MITRE ATT&CK and log summarisation, grounded in a published survey.

name: Agentic Threat Hunting Framework (ATHF)
summary: Framework for building threat-hunting systems that remember past hunts, learn from them and act with increasing autonomy.

name: seclab-taskflow-agent
summary: YAML-driven multi-agent taskflow framework from GitHub Security Lab that pairs LLM agents with CodeQL for vulnerability research.

name: Agentic-DFIR
summary: Autonomous DFIR agent for the SANS SIFT Workstation that enforces evidence-integrity rules in its architecture (typed forensic operations) rather than relying on prompts, and produces a traceable report.
notes: A sibling project page appears under the name Agentic-DART, likely an earlier name. License taken from project wiki.

name: AgentDFIR
summary: Forensics for AI agents themselves: collects and reconstructs activity from Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, Gemini CLI and Copilot, and flags orphan agents, cross-agent messaging and destructive commands. Go CLI.
notes: Different angle from other DFIR entries: it investigates AI-agent incidents.

name: ForceCode DFIR
summary: Terminal-native DFIR environment orchestrating specialised agents for artifact, memory, network, timeline and malware analysis plus reporting; its author describes it as still evolving.

name: Sentinel DFIR-CTI Agent
summary: Academic-style hybrid framework combining ML anomaly detection, rules, correlation, IOC/ATT&CK enrichment and a planned agent layer for forensics and threat intelligence.
notes: Several layers still marked as planned in its own architecture table.

name: Agentic Malware Analysis
summary: Kali-based container with 50+ RE tools and a Claude Code/Codex skill that runs a multi-phase malware-analysis workflow through Binary Ninja or Ghidra MCP backends and writes IOC-bearing reports.
notes: Seen during research via a mirror (gmh5225/agentic-malware-analysis); origin repo listed here.

name: Open-ReverseLab
summary: Reverse-engineering agent lab exposing 100+ MCP tools across Ghidra, Frida, x64dbg and Rizin, plus an executable knowledge base, for PE/APK/binary analysis and CTFs.

name: pyghidra-mcp
summary: MCP server exposing Ghidra analysis (decompile, xrefs, project-wide queries) to LLM agents with compact, token-efficient tool descriptions.

name: Anthropic-Cybersecurity-Skills (community)
summary: Large library of structured cybersecurity skills (800+ across ~30 domains) for AI agents, following the agentskills.io standard and mapped to frameworks such as MITRE ATT&CK and NIST CSF.
notes: Community project: the name uses 'Anthropic' but a third-party landscape list describes it as unofficial. Listing it does not imply Anthropic endorsement.

name: mcp-security-hub
summary: Collection of about 38 containerised MCP servers wrapping 300+ security tools for recon, web, binary analysis, cloud and fuzzing.

name: PortSwigger MCP Server
summary: Official Burp Suite extension bridging Burp with MCP clients such as Claude Desktop.

name: MetasploitMCP
summary: MCP bridge to the Metasploit Framework for module selection, payload generation and session handling from an AI client.

name: MCP-Kali-Server
summary: Lightweight API bridge, packaged in Kali's repositories, letting AI clients run tools like nmap, sqlmap and hydra for assisted testing and CTFs.

name: BloodHound-MCP-AI
summary: Natural-language interface to BloodHound: wraps Cypher queries as about 75 tools for Active Directory attack-path analysis.

name: Agentic Radar
summary: CLI scanner that maps agentic workflows (LangGraph, CrewAI, OpenAI Agents and others), their tools and data flows, and flags security risks.
notes: Reported by a third-party list to be owned by Zscaler after its Nov 2025 acquisition of SPLX.

name: Agent Threat Rules (ATR)
summary: Open detection-rule standard for AI-agent threats, positioned as Sigma for AI agents.

name: Buttercup (DARPA AIxCC)
summary: Trail of Bits' cyber reasoning system from the DARPA AI Cyber Challenge finals (2nd place) for automated vulnerability discovery and patching.

name: ATLANTIS (DARPA AIxCC)
summary: Open-sourced cyber reasoning system from the AIxCC 2025 winning team, combining fuzzing, symbolic execution and LLM agents to find and fix vulnerabilities.
